items.title: Ad Fontes: A New Look at the Watermarks on Paper Copies of the Gutenberg Bible
items.note: Re-examines paper stocks across B42 copies, refining the production sequence against which changes in the type and its casting have to be dated.

items.title: Editio Princeps: A History of the Gutenberg Bible
items.note: History and census of the 49 surviving copies and fragments of at least 14 others, the reference point for locating copies to compare.

items.title: Gutenberg
items.note: English edition of the Mainz printing historian's synthesis, with chapters on DK-type print runs and the B42 and a list of digitized Gutenberg Bibles.

items.title: Did Johannes Gutenberg invent the hand mould? Conclusions drawn from microscopic type comparisons of early prints
items.venue: JGU Mainz Open Science (English translation of Gutenberg-Jahrbuch 2015)
items.note: Microscopic comparison of letter variants in early prints, concluding they are consistent with a punch-matrix-hand-mould system, against the temporary-matrix hypothesis.

items.title: Statistical Analysis of the Gutenberg 42-line Bible Types: Special Focus on Letters with a Suspension Stroke
items.venue: Papers of the Bibliographical Society of America
items.note: Statistical measurement of letters with suspension strokes in the Keio B42 copy, read as evidence for how sorts and their matrices were made.

items.title: Princeton acquires 21 fifteenth-century printing types from Lyons
items.note: Bought at auction a group of Guillaume de Roy's types recovered from the Saône in 1868, among the very few physical fifteenth-century sorts available for study.

items.title: Two corrections to recent censuses of the Gutenberg 42-line bible
items.who: L. M. Rangel and A. Alabert
items.venue: Journal of the Printing Historical Society, n.s. 3
items.note: Corrects copy-level details in the Needham and White censuses and discusses the print-run increase, relevant to any multi-copy comparison of B42 type.

items.title: Werck der bücher: Transitions, experimentation, and collaboration in reprographic technologies, 1440-1470
items.who: S. Mossman et al. (Manchester, with Mainz and Erlangen)
items.note: AHRC-DFG project (UK share £213,395; 2021/22 to 2026) to pattern-match every movable-type edition of 1440 to 1470 and test how many distinct typecasting technologies existed.

items.title: Analysis of the Gutenberg 42-line Bible types aided by type-image recognition
items.note: OCR-assisted measurement of about 120,000 letters on 46 Keio pages; stroke-to-letter distances differ between 40- and 42-line pages, suggesting separately punched strokes.

items.title: The Typefounder's Hand Mould
items.note: Historical and practical study of surviving hand moulds and how to build and cast with one, by a maker of about fifty years' experience; useful for testing casting hypotheses.
